question: How long do States or other Federal agencies with their own MUTCDs or supplements have to revise them into substantial conformance after changes to the National MUTCD become effective?
model_answer: Direct Answer: States or other Federal agencies with their own MUTCDs or Supplements must revise them to be in substantial conformance with changes to the National MUTCD within 2 years of the effective date of the Final Rule for those changes. This requirement also extends to agency policies, directives, specifications, and similar documents that modify MUTCD provisions, which are treated as supplements. Standards (mandatory): - "States or other Federal agencies that have their own MUTCDs or Supplements shall revise these MUTCDs or Supplements to be in substantial conformance with changes to the National MUTCD within 2 years of the effective date of the Final Rule for the changes [23 CFR 655.603(b)(3)]. Substantial conformance of such State or other Federal agency MUTCDs or Supplements shall be as defined in 23 CFR 655.603(b)(1)." - "Policies, directives, specifications, standard drawings, or similar documents that are issued by an agency and that change or modify Standard, Guidance, or Option provisions in this Manual shall be considered as supplements to the MUTCD and shall also be revised to be in substantial conformance with the National MUTCD." - "After the effective date of a new edition of the MUTCD or a revision thereto, or after the adoption thereof by the State, whichever occurs later, new or reconstructed devices installed shall comply with the new edition or revision, as required by 23 CFR 655.603." Citations: - Section 1B.02 Standard §2 (p.4) - Section 1B.02 Standard §3 (p.5) - Section 1B.03 Standard §3 (p.5)
gold_answer: They must revise their MUTCDs or supplements into substantial conformance within 2 years of the effective date of the Final Rule for the changes.
